cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and David's son, starts building the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. The spot is Mount Moriah. And friend, this isn't some random lot he found scrolling his phone at midnight.

cards.question: Solomon builds the house of the LORD on Mount Moriah. What had happened on that mountain before?

answers.text: The LORD had appeared to David there
David had been anointed king there

cards.question: Solomon's building spot is the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, a place already prepared by ___.

cards.text: Solomon breaks ground on the second day of the second month of his fourth year, on a foundation sixty cubits long and twenty wide, by the old standard. The Bible remembers the exact DAY, friend, and I spent so long in a drawer I couldn't tell you the YEAR.

Then the GOLD starts: the inside of the portico, the main room, the beams, the thresholds, the walls with cherubim carved on them, even the DOORS. Friend, the fanciest thing in my old junk drawer was a coupon that expired years ago.

Then comes the Most Holy Place, and the inside alone gets six HUNDRED talents of fine gold. In there, Solomon makes two cherubim of sculptured work and overlays THEM with gold too, because apparently anything that holds still in this building gets gold on it.

cards.question: Each of the two cherubim in the Most Holy Place stretches out two wings. One wing touches the temple wall, and the other touches the ___ of the other cherub.
True or false: Wing to wing, the two cherubim reach all the way across the Most Holy Place, from wall to wall.

cards.text: The two cherubim stand on their feet, facing the main room. Then Solomon makes the veil from blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen, and friend, my apron comes in exactly one color: WHITE.

cards.question: Cherubim carved on the walls, two golden cherubim in the Most Holy Place. What does Solomon weave into the veil?

cards.text: Out front, he makes two pillars, thirty-five cubits high together, with chainwork on top and a hundred pomegranates fastened into it. A HUNDRED, friend, and I get tired topping one batch.
He sets the pillars up in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. Then he does something for them that the Millers once did for my handle.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon gives each of the two pillars in front of the temple a name.
Solomon names the two pillars in front of the temple. Which two names does he give them?

cards.text: Now the furnishings, starting with a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty wide and ten HIGH. Friend, I'm a stamper on a little gold base, and I'd need a LADDER just to see the top of this thing.
Then he makes the Sea of cast metal: round, ten cubits rim to rim, five high, with two rows of ox figures cast right below the rim. Not the Tub, not the Big Bowl, the SEA.

cards.question: The Sea doesn't sit on the ground. It rests on twelve ___, three facing each direction.

cards.text: The Sea holds three thousand baths, and Solomon adds ten basins for washing, five on the south side and five on the north, where the parts of the burnt offering get rinsed. Ten basins AND a Sea, friend, and my whole bakery runs on one sink.

cards.question: The ten basins are for rinsing the parts of the burnt offering. So who uses the Sea for washing?
True or false: Solomon makes ten gold lampstands and puts all ten together on the north side of the temple.
Solomon makes ten tables and sets them in the temple, five on each side. He also makes a hundred gold ___.

cards.text: He makes the courtyard of the priests and the large court, with bronze on the doors, and the Sea goes in at the southeast corner. Friend, I've had a whole planet to myself all this time and I STILL can't decide where the cooling rack goes.

Huram, the craftsman the king of Tyre sent (2 Chronicles 2:13), finishes the work: the pillars, the network, four hundred pomegranates, the stands, the basins, the Sea and its oxen, the pots, shovels and forks, all polished bronze cast in clay molds on the plain of the Jordan. That's Huram's to-do list, friend, and I need a nap after ONE batch.

cards.question: Solomon makes all these bronze articles in great abundance. What's the result?

answers.text: No one could figure out the weight
It used up every mine in Israel

cards.text: Now the gold: Solomon makes the golden altar and the tables for the house of God. Friend, the only gold I own is the base I'm standing on, and I am NOT stepping off it.

cards.question: What gets placed on the tables Solomon makes for the house of God?
True or false: The lampstands of pure gold and their lamps burn out in the large court.

cards.text: Last comes the rest in purest gold: flowers, lamps, tongs, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, censers, and the gold doors to the Most Holy Place and the main hall. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't done.

findings.problem: The detail-heavy temple building plans and furnishing inventories are spread across numerous cards and quizzed item by item, including the cherub measurements in stop 1 and the furnishings throughout chapter 4. Chapter 4's inventory also receives a stop of its own. These long detail stretches should be summarized in one story card each, without choice cards, within a stop containing the surrounding narrative.

rule.text: The rule: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. A stretch never gets a stop of its own. Its one card sits in the stop with the moments around it. He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards gives the baker a basis for choosing "bowls" over "cups" or "jars." The blank asks for an unseen inventory detail, so a correct pick depends on luck rather than reasoning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
